relevance_rank_note: Measures lipidated ApoE binding to the LDLR ectodomain directly (cell-surface binding at 4 C, HTRF, SPR) and then LDLR surface level, ApoE-LDLR colocalisation and LDL uptake in H4 cells and human APOE KO iPSC-derived astrocytes, so it tests both halves of H4; the isoform contrast the paper draws is ApoE2 versus ApoE3/E4, and the ApoE4 versus ApoE3 comparison is null in every binding and recycling readout except the amount of internalised ApoE.

description: Surface plasmon resonance of POPC-lipidated ApoE flowed over immobilised LDLR ectodomain gave a modestly lower dissociation constant for lipApoE4 than for lipApoE3, which the authors describe as high affinity binding for both isoforms without testing ApoE4 against ApoE3. Effect detail: KD 9 nM for lipApoE4 versus 16 nM for lipApoE3, with lipApoE2 at 800 nM.
quote: SPR similarly revealed a high affinity LDLR binding for both lipApoE4 and lipApoE3 (KD = 9 nM and 16 nM, respectively), whereas the lipApoE2-LDLR affinity was ~50-fold lower than lipApoE3 (KD = 800 nM; Figure 1D)
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (slightly lower KD for lipApoE-LDLR binding, 16 nM -> 9 nM, untested)
system: Cell-free surface plasmon resonance (Biacore 8k, C1 chip, neutravidin-coupled, biotinylated human LDLR extracellular domain immobilised at 330-360 RU); HEK293-derived human ApoE2, ApoE3 and ApoE4 lipidated with POPC, injected at 0.0156, 0.03125 and 0.0625 micromolar for lipApoE3/E4 and 0.5, 1 and 2 micromolar for lipApoE2, 60 s association and 300 s dissociation, 1:1 kinetic fit. cell-free recombinant binding assay at neutral pH with artificially POPC-lipidated ApoE and an isolated receptor ectodomain, not human brain cells.
human_check: Set against: true 2026-11-23 (team leader). The printed KDs (lipApoE4 9 nM vs lipApoE3 16 nM) run in the H4 direction, but no statistical comparison of ApoE4 against ApoE3 exists anywhere in the panel and the authors' own framing is high-affinity LDLR binding for BOTH isoforms, with the real contrast against ApoE2's roughly 50-fold lower affinity. An independent blind referee reached against on the same reading. Both KD values and the authors' framing are kept in the description so a reviewer can re-read it the other way. The two KD values are printed in the text but no statistical comparison of lipApoE4 versus lipApoE3 is reported and no replicate count is given for SPR, so P and n are N/A and the effect column is qualitative rather than a 1.8x ratio (a ratio of two KDs the authors never contrasted). The authors themselves call the two isoforms similar ('Given similar LDLR-binding by lipApoE3 and lipApoE4'), so this row should not be read as a demonstrated tighter-binding result.

description: In a homogeneous time-resolved fluorescence titration against the LDLR ectodomain, lipidated ApoE3 and ApoE4 gave superimposable binding curves with a single shared EC50 of about 13 nM, while lipApoE2 bound minimally: no ApoE4 versus ApoE3 difference in LDLR binding affinity.
quote: Conversely, lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 both exhibited high affinity binding, demonstrating a half maximum effective concentration (EC50) of ~13 nM.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LDLR binding EC50, ~13 nM for both)
system: Cell-free HTRF binding assay in 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 2 mM CaCl2, 0.1% BSA; 10 nM biotinylated human LDLR extracellular domain with 8-point two-fold dilutions of His-tagged POPC-lipidated human ApoE2/E3/E4, 1 h at room temperature, 3 separate titrations in triplicate, 4-parameter sigmoidal fit. cell-free recombinant assay at neutral pH with artificially lipidated ApoE and an isolated receptor ectodomain, not human brain cells.
human_check: Null for ApoE4 versus ApoE3: one EC50 is quoted for both isoforms, so the effect is qualitative (no magnitude for the E4 vs E3 contrast) and no test between them is reported. n = 3 independent titrations from the legend.

description: FITC-labelled lipidated ApoE was bound to the surface of LDLR-overexpressing 293T cells at 4 C, a temperature that blocks endocytosis; lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 gave similarly robust surface signals while lipApoE2 was minimal, and the only significance brackets drawn are ApoE2 against each of ApoE3 and ApoE4.
quote: Robust cell surface signals were observed for lipApoE3 and lipApoE4, while minimal signals were observed for lipApoE2, indicating reduced binding of lipApoE2 to LDLR (Figure 1A–B).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in cell-surface LDLR binding at 4 C)
system: Human 293T cells overexpressing human LDLR, incubated 1 h at 4 C with 10 micrograms/mL FITC-labelled POPC/cholesterol-lipidated human ApoE2, ApoE3 or ApoE4; confocal quantification of total signal per cell normalised to the mean, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's multiple comparisons. embryonic kidney cell line overexpressing the receptor, exogenous artificially lipidated ApoE, 4 C binding-only condition, not human brain cells.
human_check: I viewed Fig 1B: the two **** brackets both originate at the lipApoE2 bar (to lipApoE3 and to lipApoE4); there is no bracket between lipApoE3 and lipApoE4, and Dunnett's compares against a single control, so the ApoE4 versus ApoE3 comparison is not tested rather than tested-null. Bars read lipApoE3 slightly higher than lipApoE4, i.e. if anything against H4. n estimated as 3 plotted points per bar; the legend gives no n for this panel.

description: Cell-surface LDLR was immunostained after one day of lipidated ApoE treatment in human APOE knockout iPSC-derived astrocytes; lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 left surface LDLR at the same level as each other (and as no ApoE), with only lipApoE2 raising it, so ApoE4 did not impair LDLR recycling more than ApoE3.
quote: In H4, WT HAP1, and APOE KO iAstrocytes, incubation with lipApoE3/E4 significantly reduced surface LDLR relative to lipApoE2, revealing impaired LDLR recycling accompanying increased LDLR-mediated lipApoE uptake (Figure 2A–D, Figure S2A–B).
system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from an APOE epsilon3/epsilon3 line CRISPR-edited to APOE knockout, treated 1 d with 10 micrograms/mL POPC-lipidated human ApoE2, ApoE3 or ApoE4; live-cell anti-LDLR surface immunostaining, confocal total signal per cell normalised to median, one-way ANOVA with Sidak's multiple comparisons. iPSC-derived astrocytes rather than brain tissue, APOE knocked out and the isoform supplied exogenously as an artificially POPC-lipidated particle.
human_check: I viewed Fig 2D: all three **** brackets involve ApoE2 (no ApoE vs ApoE2, ApoE2 vs ApoE3, ApoE2 vs ApoE4); the ApoE3 and ApoE4 bars sit at about 0.93 and 0.95 of median with no bracket between them, and Sidak's tests only selected comparisons, so this is untested-null, recorded as against per the H2 convention. n estimated as 3 plotted points per bar.

description: Super-resolution imaging of APOE knockout iPSC-derived astrocytes after one day of lipidated ApoE treatment showed more internalised ApoE4 than ApoE3 inside the cells, with a significance bracket drawn between the ApoE3 and ApoE4 bars; internalised ApoE of every isoform colocalised completely with LDLR.
quote: ApoE isoform differences were manifested in the differential levels of internalized lipApoE (ApoE4 > ApoE3 > ApoE2), giving rise to the same isoform trend for LAMP1-positive vesicles containing ApoE immunoreactivity
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more internalised ApoE retained with LDLR in endolysosomes)
system: Human iPSC-derived astrocytes from an APOE epsilon3/epsilon3 line CRISPR-edited to APOE knockout, 1 d treatment with 10 micrograms/mL POPC-lipidated human ApoE2, ApoE3 or ApoE4; super-resolution confocal co-immunostaining of LAMP1, ApoE and LDLR, total internalised ApoE signal per cell normalised to median, one-way ANOVA with Sidak's multiple comparisons. iPSC-derived astrocytes with APOE knocked out and exogenous artificially lipidated ApoE; the readout is the amount of ApoE taken up, not a measurement of ApoE-LDLR affinity or of LDLR recycling.
human_check: I viewed Fig 2I (left graph): the single-star bracket runs from the ApoE3 bar to the ApoE4 bar (the ** bracket is ApoE2 to ApoE4), so the <0.05 inequality from the legend key (*p < 0.05) does belong to the ApoE4 versus ApoE3 contrast. Effect left qualitative rather than estimated: bars are about 1.25 versus 2.2 of median, but that is a ratio of two normalised arbitrary-unit means and the authors print no magnitude for this contrast. n estimated as 3 plotted points per bar. Direction supports more ApoE4 uptake/retention, which is B-adjacent but is not evidence of tighter adhesion by itself.

description: DiI-LDL uptake in serum-starved H4 cells was inhibited to the same extent by lipApoE3 and lipApoE4, both in co-treatment and after one day of ApoE pre-treatment, where uptake was nearly abolished by either isoform; only lipApoE2 behaved differently.
quote: both lipApoE3 and lipApoE4 led to 60–65% inhibition of DiI-LDL uptake, likely via a direct competition with LDL for LDLR binding, whereas lipApoE2 had no effect (Figure 2J, L)
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in LDLR-mediated DiI-LDL uptake inhibition)
system: Human H4 neuroglioma cells, serum-starved, co-treated 3-4 h with 10 micrograms/mL POPC-lipidated human ApoE2/E3/E4 and 10 micrograms/mL DiI-LDL, or pre-treated 1 d with lipApoE before 3-4 h DiI-LDL; confocal DiI signal per cell as a fraction of no-ApoE, two-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons. neuroglioma cell line, exogenous artificially lipidated ApoE, and the readout is competition for ligand uptake rather than receptor recycling or ApoE-receptor affinity.
human_check: The printed 60-65% is lipApoE3/E4 versus no ApoE, not an ApoE4 versus ApoE3 magnitude, so the effect column for this contrast is qualitative. I viewed Fig 2L: the **** brackets are ApoE2 or no-ApoE against ApoE3/ApoE4 and between treatment regimes; no ApoE3-to-ApoE4 bracket is drawn and Tukey bars shown are selected, so the E4 vs E3 null is untested. n estimated as 3 plotted points per bar.
